items.title: Is Your Long-Horizon Benchmark Really Deep? Measuring and Synthesizing Depth in Terminal Tasks

items.summary_1line: Multimodal web agents have shown promising capabilities for interacting with websites through graphical user interfaces (GUIs), yet realistic web tasks often require long-horizon, multi-step planning that remains chal...
items.editor_note: JHiMA-WebRL trains hierarchical multi-agent policies jointly for long-horizon web tasks.

editorial.tldr: Mid-October arXiv papers began framing long-horizon agent work around research-state tracking and continual-learning benchmarks. Late October added search evaluation with failure localization, critic-based credit assignment, and memory governance.
editorial.whats_new: JHiMA-WebRL applies joint hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning to long-horizon web tasks, following a paper questioning whether long-horizon terminal benchmarks are actually deep.
editorial.why_it_matters: Long-horizon failures (lost state, stale memory, weak credit assignment) are what break production agents; this cluster shows research moving from raw task length toward diagnosing where trajectories fail.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you evaluate long-running agents, track failure nodes and memory staleness rather than turn counts alone; these are unreplicated preprints, so rerun on your own tasks before adopting any method.
